answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in river, which means the distribution is public, and prism lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a dune header, so 3323 keys running one model collapse to a single share. The fee repeats 28 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
